Fold the alpha-profiling sub-pool back into training

fold_alpha_test_to_train.Rd

Once \(\alpha\) has been estimated by estimate_group_alpha, the sub-pool of sampleSet == "test" trials it reserved for profiling \(\alpha\) (alpha_test_rows, part of its return value) has no further job to do – \(\alpha\) is now a fixed number, not something being estimated from anything. Holding that sub-pool out of training any longer is pure waste: there is nothing left for it to stay independent from. This function sets sampleSet <- "train" at exactly those rows (and no others – in particular, the remaining test_fit sub-pool is left as "test", since it still has a job: governing early stopping for the one last fit at the now-fixed \(\alpha\)).

Usage

fold_alpha_test_to_train(triplet_list, alpha_test_rows)

Arguments

triplet_list

A named or unnamed list of per-participant data frames, each with a sampleSet column – the same object passed to estimate_group_alpha.

alpha_test_rows

Integer vector, typically estimate_group_alpha(...)$alpha_test_rows from a call on this same triplet_list: positions (1-based) into do.call(rbind, triplet_list) to flip from "test" to "train".

Value

triplet_list with sampleSet updated at alpha_test_rows; a list of the same length, names, and row order as the input. No other column, and no other row's sampleSet, is touched.

Why this is a mechanical flip, not a re-derivation

alpha_test_rows must come from a call to estimate_group_alpha on this exact same triplet_list (same participants, same row order within each). This function does not re-run any random split itself – it just flips sampleSet at the positions it's given – so there is no risk of drifting out of sync with what \(\alpha\) was actually profiled on, the way independently re-deriving an equivalent split (e.g. replaying sample_internal_test a second time with the same seed) would risk if any upstream detail ever changed.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
grp <- run_group_embedding_from_list(icon_triplets, d = 3L)
joint <- estimate_group_alpha(icon_triplets, warm_start = grp$embedding)
folded <- fold_alpha_test_to_train(icon_triplets, joint$alpha_test_rows)
# Now fit the real final embedding at (d, joint$alpha) on `folded`,
# e.g. with several random-seed restarts, keeping the lowest test loss.
} # }
